subject: Acceptance gates, success metrics & responsibility register — FastRetail POC next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance gates, success metrics & responsibility register — FastRetail POC next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth as we scope the 6-week POC: 

Summary of ask:
- Validate Redwood inference latency and cost vs. your current endpoint for the product search reranking flow (avg doc length ~350 tokens).
- Measure end-to-end throughput at 50 concurrent active sessions with 95th pct latency <= 300ms.
- Confirm data handling meets your security requirements (no customer PII persisted in host).

Draft success metrics (spreadsheet attached):
1) Latency: 95th pct per-request < 300ms for 75% of runs across a 48-hour load window.
2) Cost: token cost reduction >=15% vs current baseline (p50).
3) Quality: NDCG@10 delta within ±2% of current production.
4) Reliability: sustained throughput >=50 concurrent sessions with <1% error rate.

Proposed ownership/RACI (high-level):
- Technical owner (Redwood): Ben Carter — infra tuning, model variant recommendations, test harness.
- Application owner (FastRetail): Alex Green — sample payloads, feature toggle for traffic routing.
- Security/compliance (joint): Kimberly Park (Redwood) & FastRetail security (Priya) — dataflow review and encryption/KMS validation.
- Procurement/legal (FastRetail): procurement@fastretail.com — SOW and PO timeline.

Immediate next steps:
1) Ben to share test harness and sampling guidance (by Wed 7/2).
2) FastRetail to provide 1 week of representative logs and a small labeled eval set (by Fri 7/4).
3) Sign SOW v0.2 and confirm start date (we attached a draft).

Attachments: FastRetail_POC_Success_Metrics.xlsx, FastRetail_SOW_v0.2.pdf

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Kimberly to start the security checklist and Marissa to set up a weekly cadence.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0192
From: Alex Green <alex.green@fastretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@fastretail.com>, procurement@fastretail.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 17:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance gates, success metrics & responsibility register — FastRetail POC next steps

Sean — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock timelines: 

1) The 50 concurrent sessions number is correct but note peak bursts hit 120 for short windows during promotions — can Redwood simulate burst behavior or should we plan a separate stress test?
2) For quality, we usually run A/B over a 3-day window; is the 48-hour load window you mention separate from the quality eval period?
3) Security: Priya will lead but wants to confirm whether Redwood can sign our standard NDA addendum and share a data flow diagram before any data transfer.

I'll push to get the logs and small eval set by Fri 7/4 but procurement will need the SOW and a payment cadence to align with our quarter close. I've CC'd procurement.

—Alex
Alex Green
Head of ML Ops, FastRetail
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@fastretail.com>, procurement@fastretail.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance gates, success metrics & responsibility register — FastRetail POC next steps

Thanks Alex — good questions. Answers and updates below: 

1) Burst testing: Ben can run a targeted stress test to simulate 120-concurrency bursts. Proposal: baseline 48-hour steady-state run + two 30-min burst tests at end of day 2. Ben — can you confirm tooling and expected extra cost?

2) Quality eval window: yes — keep NDCG/CTR quality measurements over a 72-hour A/B window; latency/throughput objectives measured during steady-state 48-hour interval. We’ll capture both but treat the metrics independently for pass/fail gates.

3) NDA/addendum & data flow: Kimberly will pick up the privacy addendum and share a dataflow diagram. Kimberly — can you confirm we can sign FastRetail’s addendum and provide a draft diagram by EOD Wed 7/2?

Procurement — noted on payment cadence. Marissa will follow up with your team to agree on SOW terms and invoice milestones. Marissa — can you queue the SOW for signature and give an estimated timeline?

I’ll attach an updated timeline once Ben confirms the test plan.

Sean

Date: Wed, 2 Jul 2025 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance gates, success metrics & responsibility register — FastRetail POC next steps

Alex / team — quick status from security/compliance side: 

- We reviewed FastRetail’s standard NDA addendum. Legal is OK to sign with the following clarifications (1) Redwood will not persist raw customer PII; (2) we’ll use customer-owned KMS for any key material. I’ll circulate a signed copy by EOD.

- Dataflow diagram: attached (stub). It shows ingest -> transient KV caching -> inference -> no-disk logging (metrics only). If you want host-side log redaction rules, list the fields and we’ll implement them in the harness.

- Checklist items I need from FastRetail to complete:
  * Representative payload schema (JSON) and sample messages (anonymized)
  * Contact for KMS/crypto team (name + email)
  * Any regulatory constraints (PCI/SO/other) beyond standard retail PII handling

Ben — I’ll coordinate with you on required infra access and port/IP allowlist.

Attachments: FastRetail_Dataflow_Diagram.png (diagram stub)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Lead Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Green <alex.green@fastretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Sean / Kimberly / team — thanks for the fast turnaround. Procurement confirms they can review SOW v0.2 and aim to return a signed PO by Wed 7/9 provided the payment cadence is net-30. I've asked our KMS contact (Priya) to introduce the crypto lead — she should be on the thread shortly.

On burst testing: we’re fine with the steady-state + two short bursts. Please include a short appendix in the SOW describing the burst test and any incremental costs.

I’ll upload a 72-hour anonymized sample payload set to the shared drive (link below) by EOD. 

Thanks,
Alex
